issues.legal_issue: The exemption for an occupied residential house from attachment and sale in civil decree execution does not apply to statutory revenue-recovery proceedings unless the governing statute makes that exemption applicable.
material_facts: A licensee defaulted on a fee owed to the State, and recovery proceedings were initiated under a land revenue statute.
An authorized officer attached and notified for auction the licensee’s share in property that included a building partly used as his residence.
The licensee claimed that the residential portion was exempt under a civil-procedure provision, but the land revenue statute did not adopt that provision or provide a corresponding exemption.
issues.conclusion: The civil-procedure exemption did not apply to the attachment and sale in the revenue-recovery proceedings. The residential share was not exempt on that basis, so the appeal was allowed and the lower courts’ dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, sections 2(2) and 60(1), including the proviso’s clause (ccc) as amended for Punjab, concern attachment and sale in execution of a civil court decree. The phrase “such attachment or sale” in the proviso refers to the attachment and sale described in section 60(1). Those provisions do not apply to proceedings under another statute unless that statute expressly makes them applicable. Under the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887, the recovery process was governed by that Act, which neither adopted section 60 nor provided a corresponding residential-house exemption. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: revenue_recovery_proceeding and attachment_not_civil_decree_execution and no_express_adoption_of_civil_exemptions and no_equivalent_residential_exemption

predicates.revenue_recovery_proceeding: Public dues were sought to be recovered through statutory revenue-recovery proceedings.
predicates.attachment_not_civil_decree_execution: The attachment and proposed sale were carried out under the revenue-recovery process rather than in execution of a civil court decree.
predicates.no_express_adoption_of_civil_exemptions: The law governing the recovery proceedings did not expressly make civil decree-execution exemptions applicable to those proceedings.
predicates.no_equivalent_residential_exemption: The law governing the recovery proceedings contained no exemption corresponding to the protection for an occupied residential house in civil decree execution.

issues.definition: When public dues are pursued through statutory revenue-recovery proceedings, the attachment is not in execution of a civil decree, and the governing law adopts no corresponding residential exemption, residential property is not exempt from attachment and sale on that basis.
